newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ clears Bulmer buy of cidermaker Harvest.
newsitem.headline: NZ clears Bulmer buy of cidermaker Harvest.

text.p: New Zealand's monopolies panel, the Commerce Commission, said on Wednesday it had cleared Bulmer Trading (NZ) Ltd's proposed purchase of the cider making assets of Harvest Wine Company Limited.
Bulmer Trading is owned by Britain's biggest cidermaker H.P. Bulmer Plc and the purchase would give it control of New Zealand's biggest producer, but not dominant market share, the Commission said.
It said it had concluded the merged firm would have less than 60 percent of the relevant market and face competition from at least one rival with a market share of 15 percent or more.
Harvest produces, distributes and exports Harvest brand cider and produces the Stonehouse brand under contract to New Zealand Breweries.

The proposed deal, of which financial details were not initially available, involves Bulmer buying Harvest's cider making assets and undertaking, and its goodwill. It does not involve Harvest's sparkling juice, wine and mead business.
